npcs.name: Lord Aubrec Valmont
npcs.greet: A knight of the Rose is courteous to the poor, honest with the powerful and terrible to the wicked. Most days I manage two of the three.

npcs.name: Dame Orielle Fontaine
npcs.greet: Manners first, then the sword. You'd be amazed how many fights end at the manners.

npcs.name: Chancellor Ivo Brennault
npcs.greet: The King is very busy. I am very busy on his behalf. Speak quickly, and beautifully if you can manage it.

npcs.name: Sir Garrick Vane
npcs.greet: I serve the Chancellor. That is all you need to know about me, and more than most people learn.

npcs.name: Elsabet Mornay
npcs.greet: Father sits on the King's council. Everyone is very polite to me, and nobody tells me anything.

relics.name: Ransom Letter
relics.desc: A demand for five thousand crowns for the safe return of Elsabet Mornay. Written in a careful hand, on very good paper. Pirates rarely own very good paper.

relics.name: Purse of New Crowns
relics.desc: Freshly minted Wayrest coin, still in the wrapping of the banker who serves the Chancellor's household.

kr_the_yield: Sir Garrick lies in the sand of the duelling ground with his helm knocked askew. The crowd is silent. In the gallery, the Chancellor's chair is empty.
The trial is decided. Before Stendarr and the court of Wayrest, the Chancellor's cause has failed. Guards, find him.
kr_roses_oath: In the chapel of the Rose, every knight in Wayrest stands with a white rose pinned over the heart. The candles have burned low.
We swear to keep faith with the weak, to speak truth to the mighty and to suffer no cruelty in our sight. You have kept that oath before you ever spoke it.
Say the words, and take the rose. The order is yours to lead in the field, as Lord of the Rose.

quests.title: A Courteous Blade
quests.offer: I'd like to earn a place among the Knights of the Rose.
quests.pitch: Then begin where we all begin, with the people nobody else bothers about. A gang has been squeezing coin out of the fishwives on the Wayrest docks. Dame Orielle will tell you more. Settle it, and settle it like a knight, not a brawler.
quests.desc: Lord Aubrec Valmont of the Knights of the Rose set me a first task: end the extortion of the fishwives on the Wayrest docks.

objectives.topic: Lord Valmont sent me about the docks.
objectives.reply: The Gullhook boys. They sell 'protection' to women who gut fish for a living, and break their tables when they can't pay. Give them the chance to leave. If they refuse it, don't give them a second.

objectives.text: Break the Gullhook gang on the docks
objectives.journal: I told them to leave the docks. Their leader laughed and drew a gutting knife. The fishwives cheered at the end, which I did not expect.

objectives.topic: The Gullhook gang won't trouble anyone again.
objectives.reply: I watched from the harbour wall. You offered them the door first. Good. That's what separates us from the men we fight. Go and tell Lord Valmont.
Dame Orielle has already sung your praises, which she does about once a decade. Take the Rose, Aspirant. Wear it where people can see it, and behave accordingly.

quests.outro: I broke the Gullhook gang that preyed on the fishwives of the Wayrest docks. Lord Aubrec Valmont accepted me as an aspirant of the Knights of the Rose.

quests.title: Very Good Paper
quests.pitch: I am. Iliac Bay pirates have taken Elsabet Mornay, whose father sits on the King's council. Chancellor Brennault wants the ransom paid quietly and quickly. Something about it smells wrong. Go and see the Chancellor, and look at that letter with a knight's eyes.
quests.desc: Pirates have kidnapped Elsabet Mornay, daughter of a royal councillor. Chancellor Ivo Brennault wants the ransom paid at once, and Lord Valmont suspects something is wrong.

objectives.topic: Lord Valmont asked me to look at the ransom letter.
objectives.reply: Valmont asked, did he? Very well. Read it, by all means. The girl's life is on a clock, and the Rose should be helping me pay, not reading over my shoulder. The money goes to the docks tonight.

objectives.text: Catch the go-between collecting the ransom on the docks
objectives.journal: The go-between was no pirate. He wore a clerk's ink stains under his sailor's coat, and he fought like a man who had never expected to.

objectives.text: Take the purse the go-between carried
Bring the purse and the letter to Lord Valmont
objectives.topic: The go-between was carrying this. It's the Chancellor's own coin.
objectives.reply: Paid to the pirates by the Chancellor's banker, before the ransom was ever announced. Brennault arranged this himself. The question is why. We need the girl back before anyone thinks to silence her.

quests.outro: The ransom for Elsabet Mornay was being paid out of Chancellor Brennault's own purse before the kidnapping was announced. The Chancellor arranged it. Lord Valmont wants her rescued before she can be silenced.

quests.title: The Saltreef Hostage
quests.desc: Elsabet Mornay is held by pirates at Saltreef Hold on the coast west of Wayrest. Lord Valmont wants her brought home alive before the Chancellor's allies decide she knows too much.

objectives.text: Fight through the pirates of Saltreef Hold
Kill the pirate captain, Red Brannoc
objectives.journal: Red Brannoc told me, with his last breath, that he had been paid to take the girl and paid again to keep her. He didn't say by whom. He didn't need to.

objectives.topic: Lord Valmont sent me. You're safe now.
objectives.reply: I heard them talking about the Chancellor. My father was going to vote against his new tariff. They were going to hold me until the council met. Please, take me home.

objectives.topic: Elsabet is home. She heard the pirates name the Chancellor.
objectives.reply: A councillor's daughter stolen to buy a vote. The King must hear it, from her own mouth, before the whole court.

quests.outro: I rescued Elsabet Mornay from the pirates of Saltreef Hold. She heard them name Chancellor Brennault, who had her taken to force her father's vote on the King's council.

quests.title: Trial by Combat
quests.desc: Accused before the court, Chancellor Brennault claimed the old Breton right of trial by combat, and named Sir Garrick Vane his champion. Lord Valmont has named me champion of the Rose.

objectives.topic: The Chancellor wants a trial by combat?
objectives.reply: An old law, and he knows Garrick Vane has never lost a duel. If his champion wins, Stendarr has judged him innocent, and nobody may speak of it again. I am too old to be sure of beating Vane. You are not.

objectives.text: Tell Lord Valmont how you will fight

choices.label: I'll fight to make him yield. The truth needs a winner, not a corpse.
choices.reply: That is the Rose's way, and the harder one. Vane will not offer you the same courtesy.

choices.label: Whatever it takes. Vane chose his master.
choices.reply: Then go with Stendarr, and don't let anger make you careless.

objectives.text: Defeat Sir Garrick Vane on the duelling ground
objectives.journal: Garrick Vane was the best swordsman I have ever faced. When he went down he did not ask for mercy. He simply looked up at the gallery, and saw his master's chair empty.

objectives.topic: The Chancellor fled before the duel ended.
objectives.reply: Through a servants' door with half the treasury's seals in his pockets, and a pirate ship waiting at Saltreef, no doubt. He has run to the only friends he has left.

quests.outro: I defeated Sir Garrick Vane in a trial by combat, and the court of Wayrest judged the Chancellor guilty. Brennault fled before the verdict, toward his pirate allies at Saltreef.

quests.title: The Rose's Oath
quests.desc: Chancellor Ivo Brennault has fled to Saltreef Hold to sail out of the King's reach. Lord Valmont has given me the honour of bringing him to justice.

objectives.text: Cut down the Chancellor's hired swords on the shore
Stop Ivo Brennault before he reaches the ship
objectives.journal: The Chancellor was a battlemage in his youth, it turns out, and had kept his hand in. It did not save him. The pirate ship sailed without him.

objectives.text: Return to Lord Valmont in Wayrest
objectives.topic: The Chancellor won't trouble the court again.
objectives.reply: Then Wayrest owes you its honour twice over. Come to the chapel tonight. The order has a question to ask you, and an oath to hear.

quests.outro: I stopped Chancellor Brennault at Saltreef before he could escape across the bay. In the chapel of the Rose I swore the order's oath, and Lord Valmont named me Lord of the Rose.
